# Add-on (Extension) Development

The execution model is in `blender-core`. Start from `assets/addon_template/` (validated, built, and registered in CI): `blender_manifest.toml`, `__init__.py`, `operators.py`, `ui.py`.

## Procedure
1. Copy the template, then set `id` (lowercase_underscores, permanent), `name`, `tagline` (no trailing period, ≤ 64 chars), `maintainer`, `version` (semver), `license` (SPDX, GPL-3.0-or-later for code using bpy), and `blender_version_min = "4.2.0"` or higher if you use newer APIs (e.g. `"5.2.0"` for the GN `properties.inputs` API).
2. Write classes with the prefix convention `MYTOOL_OT_x` (operator), `_PT_` (panel), `_MT_` (menu), `_PG_` (property group), `_AP_` (preferences), `_UL_` (UI list). `bl_idname` for operators is `my_tool.verb_noun`.
3. Validate and build:
   ```
   blender --command extension validate ./my_tool
   blender --command extension build --source-dir ./my_tool --output-dir ./dist
   blender --command extension install-file -r user_default -e ./dist/my_tool-1.0.0.zip
   ```
4. Test headless: register the package in-process, call operators with `temp_override`, and assert on data (see `tests/test_addon.py` in this repo).

## Rules (extension-era, 5.x)
- **Relative imports only** (`from . import ops`). The package name is decided by Blender, so preferences use `bl_idname = __package__`.
- No `bl_info` (it's ignored for extensions). Everything goes in the manifest.
- **No network or file access at import/register time.** Declare `[permissions]` (`files`, `network`, `clipboard`, `camera`, `microphone`) with a reason. Check `bpy.app.online_access` before any network call.
- **Third-party Python packages**: ship `.whl` files in `./wheels/` and list them under `wheels = [...]`. Never `pip install` at runtime. Platform-specific wheels require `platforms = [...]`.
- **Properties (5.0+)**: `bpy.props` values are attributes, not dict entries (`scene["my_prop"]` no longer reaches them). For read-only props use `options={'READ_ONLY'}`. `get_transform`/`set_transform` adapt values while keeping storage. Register with `PointerProperty(type=PG)` on an ID type, and `del` it on unregister.
- **Operators**: `bl_options={"REGISTER","UNDO"}` for undo plus a redo panel. `poll()` guards the context. Return `{"FINISHED"}`/`{"CANCELLED"}`. `self.report({"WARNING"}, msg)` for user feedback. Don't call other operators in loops if a data API exists.
- **UI**: `layout.use_property_split = True` gives modern alignment. Panels in the N-panel use `bl_region_type="UI"` + `bl_category`. Append menu entries with `VIEW3D_MT_*.append(func)` and remove them on unregister.
- **Unregister** everything in reverse order (classes, props, menus, handlers, timers, keymaps, draw handlers). Leaks break reloading.
- **Drawing** (overlays): `gpu` module + `gpu_extras.batch`. `bgl` was removed in 5.0. Textures come from `gpu.texture.from_image(img)`. For scene-linear images use `draw_texture_2d(..., is_scene_linear_with_rec709_srgb_target=True)`.
- **Long tasks**: a modal operator with a timer (`wm.event_timer_add`), or `bpy.app.timers.register` with chunked work. Never block the UI for seconds.
- **Handlers**: decorate persistent ones with `@bpy.app.handlers.persistent`. Keep them cheap (they run every frame/depsgraph update).
- **Keymaps**: add them to `wm.keyconfigs.addon`, store `(km, kmi)` pairs, and remove them on unregister.
- **Translations / i18n**: `bpy.app.translations.register(__package__, dict)`.

## Publishing (extensions.blender.org)
The Blender ID account uploads the built zip. Requirements: a valid manifest, a GPL-compatible license, no obfuscated code, no bundled binaries without source, and permissions declared. Screenshots/README go on the website listing. Update with a higher `version`.

## Gotchas
- `context.scene` inside a draw function can be `None` in some editors. Guard it.
- Storing Blender data references (`bpy.types.ID`) in Python globals crashes after undo or file load. Store names or `session_uid`, and look them up again.
- `bpy.utils.register_class` fails if annotations use `=` instead of `:` for properties.
- 5.0 made several bundled modules private (`rna_info`, `bl_ui_utils`...). Don't import them.
- 5.1 no longer loads the user site-packages by default. Bundle wheels instead of relying on user installs.
- 5.2: `PreferencesFilePaths.active_asset_library` indices are offset (the "All"/"Essentials" entries come first). `UILayout.template_palette(color=)` is removed. New: `UILayout.link`, `UILayout.textbox`, `bpy.data.all_ids`, `Window.screenshot`.

# Animation

The execution model is in `blender-core` (its `references/bpy-patterns.md` has verified keyframe/driver snippets). Rigs are in `blender-character-rigging`.

## 5.x data model (what changed)
- An **Action** holds **slots** (one per animated ID) and **layers → strips → channelbags → F-curves**. A single action can animate several objects (e.g. a rig and its camera) through different slots.
- Assign: `ob.animation_data.action = act`, then make sure `ob.animation_data.action_slot` is set (picked automatically when a suitable slot exists; otherwise `act.slots.new(id_type="OBJECT", name=ob.name)`).
- F-curves: `cb = anim_utils.action_ensure_channelbag_for_slot(act, slot)`, then `cb.fcurves.ensure(path, index=i, group_name=...)`. `action.fcurves` **no longer exists**.
- The simplest route is still `pb.keyframe_insert("rotation_quaternion", frame=f)`, which creates the action, slot and channelbag.

## Workflow (keyframe animation, studio style)
1. **Blocking**: key poses on every channel (`CONSTANT` interpolation, `bpy.context.preferences.edit.keyframe_new_interpolation_type`) on golden frames (contact, down, passing, up for walks).
2. **Breakdowns**: add in-betweens that define arcs and spacing.
3. **Spline**: switch to `BEZIER`, fix spacing in the Graph Editor, and clean overshoot. Auto-clamped handles avoid overshoot.
4. **Polish**: offsets/overlap (follow-through on hair, tails, cloth bones), arcs, moving holds (never a perfectly frozen character), and contact stability (feet locked with IK).
5. **Review**: MCP `look(mode="frames", frame_count=8)` or a Workbench playblast (`blender-rendering`).

## Game animation rules
- **One action per clip**, named `<Rig>_<Clip>` or just `<Clip>`, with a fake user so it survives saving.
- **Loops**: first and last frames identical. Export frames 1..N and let the engine drop the duplicate, or exclude the last frame (UE/Unity "loop pose" options). An F-curve `CYCLES` modifier helps preview but **doesn't export**, so bake it. Verify with `scripts/loop_check.py -- --object RIG --action Walk [--root-motion root] [--fix]`: it reports pose **pops** (last ≠ first, per bone, in deg/m) and speed **hitches** across the seam, and `--fix` keys the first-frame values on the last frame (root travel is kept).
- **FPS**: author at 30 (or 24) and let engines resample. Set `scene.render.fps` before importing mocap.
- **Root motion**: the root bone carries the translation (and yaw). The hips keep the bob/sway. `scripts/bake_action.py --root-motion xy` moves the hips' ground motion to the root. In-place clips: the root stays at the origin.
- **Additive/overlay** clips (aim offsets, breathing) are exported as normal clips and marked additive in the engine.
- Keep the bone transform channels the engine expects. **Don't animate bone scale** unless the engine supports it (Roblox and many mobile pipelines don't).

## Bake control rig → export skeleton
```
scripts/bake_action.py -- --list
scripts/bake_action.py -- --source RIG_Body --target GAME_RIG_Body [--actions Walk Run] [--root-motion xy --hips spine]
```
This gives one baked action per clip (`GAME_RIG_Body|Walk`), cleaned, with fake users, plus one muted NLA track per clip (`CLIP_Walk`) so FBX (`bake_anim_use_nla_strips`/all actions) and glTF (`ACTIONS` mode) export every clip. The target's constraints are muted afterward so it plays the baked data; run `--follow` to drive it live again. Self-bake (IK/constraints → keys on the same rig): `--source X --target X`.

## Mocap and retargeting
- Import: `bpy.ops.import_anim.bvh(filepath=..., global_scale=0.01 if cm else 1, rotate_mode="NATIVE", update_scene_fps=True)`, `import_scene.fbx` (Mixamo, `automatic_bone_orientation=True`).
- Retarget: `scripts/retarget.py -- --source Mocap --target GAME_RIG [--map auto|map.json] [--in-place] [--name Walk]`. Each target bone gets the source bone's **world rotation change from rest** on its own rest orientation, so rolls, bone axes, Y-up/cm FBX object transforms and proportions don't matter. The hips travel is scaled by the hips-height ratio. Keys go straight into a new `TARGET|Name` action (quaternion, linear, fake user). Measured on a Mixamo-style rig (Y-up, 0.01 scale, rolled) → Rigify-named rig with 15% longer legs: 17 bones, < 0.1° error.
- The auto map understands Mixamo (`mixamorig:LeftUpLeg`), Rigify `DEF-`/`ORG-`, UE/Unity/BVH-style names, and spine chains of different lengths. Check it first with `--show-map` (`unmapped_key_parts` must be empty), and pass a JSON `{target: source}` for anything custom (fingers, props).
- **Rest poses must match** (T vs A matters most): pose the target's rest like the source's first. Then clean, add root motion, and export with `bake_action.py`.
- Clean mocap: decimate keys (`graph.decimate`, ratio 0.3–0.5), use an F-curve `SMOOTH` modifier or the Butterworth filter (`graph.butterworth_smooth`), and fix foot sliding with IK pins and then bake.
- Production retarget tools: Auto-Rig Pro (paid), Rokoko (free), and the engine-side retargeters (UE IK Retargeter, Unity Humanoid).

## NLA and pose library
- NLA: push actions down as strips (`track.strips.new(name, start, action)`) to layer/blend clips (blend type `REPLACE`/`ADD`/`COMBINE`), and use Tweak mode to edit. Strips need an action slot set when the action has several slots (`strip.action_slot`).
- The pose library (bundled `pose_library`) stores poses as **assets**: `poselib.create_pose_asset(pose_name=...)`, `poselib.apply_pose_asset` / `blend_pose_asset`. Use it for hand shapes, face poses, and a T/A rest pose.

## Shape keys and other properties
Any property can be keyed: `kb.keyframe_insert("value", frame=f)` (shape key), `mat.node_tree.nodes[...].inputs[...].keyframe_insert("default_value")` (materials, which engines usually ignore), custom props `ob.keyframe_insert('["prop"]')`.

## Gotchas
- `pb.matrix = ...` followed by `keyframe_insert` needs the right `scene.frame_set(f)` **first**, or an evaluation overwrites the pose.
- Connected bones (`use_connect`) can't translate. Hips/pelvis must be unconnected from the root.
- `bake_action` with visual keying reads **evaluated** poses, so constraints, IK and drivers are all captured. Mute the target's own constraints afterward (the script does), or they keep overriding the keys.
- Quaternion vs Euler: game bones should use `QUATERNION` (no gimbal lock, smooth slerp). Euler is fine for single-axis controls. Don't mix modes between keys.
- glTF sampling: `export_force_sampling` bakes every frame (the safe default). Non-linear F-curve modifiers and drivers only export when sampled.

# Asset QA (review gate)

Never assume a generated or edited mesh is correct. Check it with numbers, then look at it.

## Procedure
1. **Automated check**, passing one asset's objects together:
   `scripts/qa_check.py -- --objects Body Head Hat --profile game`
   Profiles: `game` (default), `render` (lenient), `print` (watertight required), `roblox` (20k tris/mesh, watertight, no n-gons, ≤4 influences).
2. **Fix every `errors` entry** (table below), then re-run until `"pass": true`. Each warning must be either fixed or explicitly accepted, with the reason reported to the user.
3. **Visual check, always**:
   - Live: MCP `look` with `mode="angles"` on the targets, once in `material`/`solid` shading and once in `wireframe`. Use `xray` for internals.
   - Headless: `scripts/review_shots.py -- --objects ... --mode random` (one color per object, which makes detached pieces obvious), then `--mode wire` for topology. Open the returned PNG.
4. Report: tris per object, issues fixed, and remaining accepted warnings.

## What each finding means → fix
| Finding | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `zfighting` A<->B | two surfaces facing the same way within `--eps` (1 mm) that overlap | delete the hidden duplicate, or offset ≥ 2–5 mm along the normal, or boolean/merge them |
| `back_to_back` | faces touching with opposite normals (boxes glued face-to-face) | delete the hidden faces (wasted tris, bake artifacts) |
| `floating` | island/object not touching any other part within `--tol` | move it to make contact (snap), bridge it, or join and merge. If floating is intended (sparks, UI), check it separately |
| `enclosed` | part fully inside another, not touching (eyes, internal mechanics) | usually fine. Confirm it's intended |
| `inside_out_islands` | closed part with normals pointing in | `mesh.normals_make_consistent(inside=False)` on that part |
| `inconsistent_normals_edges` | neighbouring faces wound in opposite directions | recalc normals; if it persists, look for non-manifold seams |
| `nonmanifold_edges` / `wire_edges` | >2 faces per edge, or stray edges | dissolve/delete the extra faces; `delete_loose` |
| `boundary_edges` | open holes (bad for print/Roblox/bakes) | fill (`fill_holes`/`edge_face_add`) or cap |
| `degenerate_faces` / `zero_length_edges` | collapsed geometry | `dissolve_degenerate(threshold=1e-4)` |
| `duplicate_verts` | unwelded seams | `remove_doubles(threshold=1e-4)` (Merge by Distance); check UV seams after |
| `ngons` | faces with >4 sides | triangulate/quadrangulate locally; n-gons are fine only on flat hard-surface faces that never deform |
| unapplied/negative scale | object transform | `transform_apply(rotation=True, scale=True)`; negative scale flips normals on export |
| `uv_maps: 0` / zero-area UV / overlap | missing or bad unwrap | `blender-retopology-uv` |
| unweighted / >4 influences | skinning | `blender-character-rigging` (`rig_check.py`) |
| `ground_z` ≠ 0 | asset floats or sinks | move the origin to the bottom and set z = 0 (props) |
| faces on empty/missing slot | material removed or index out of range | assign a material; engines show grey/magenta |
| `feeds [...] but is sRGB` | normal/roughness/metal/AO map tagged as color | `image.colorspace_settings.is_data = True` (Non-Color) |
| missing texture file | broken path, unpacked | relink (`blender-scene-setup` path cleanup) or pack |
| unused slot / Non-Color base color | leftovers, wrong tag | remove the slot; base color and emission are sRGB |

## Manual checks the script can't fully judge
- **Silhouette and proportions** at the target camera distance. Compare with references and real-world size (`ob.dimensions`).
- **Shading artifacts**: smoothing on hard edges (needs sharp edges/weighted normals), and pinching at poles on curved surfaces.
- **Intersections that look wrong** (a leg clipping a seat), even though they're "attached".
- **Interior/hidden geometry** that wastes tris (use `xray`).
- **Deformation**: pose the rig at extremes (elbow 140°, knee 150°, shoulder raised) and look for collapsing volume.
- **Material assignment**: slots and color spaces are checked automatically. Still look at whether each part got the *intended* material.

## Tuning
- `--eps` is the z-fight distance. Raise it to 0.005 for large environment scenes, and lower it to 0.0002 for tiny jewelry.
- `--tol` is the contact tolerance for detached parts. Raise it for chunky kitbash.
- `--no-modifiers` checks the base mesh. By default the evaluated (modifier) result is checked, which is what gets exported.
- Above `--max-tris` (300k), the z-fight and floating checks are skipped. Check high-poly sources per part instead.

# Character Rigging

The execution model is in `blender-core`. Faces and shape keys are in `blender-facial-shapekeys`, animation in `blender-animation`.

## Pipeline (scripts chain; each returns JSON)
1. **Prepare the mesh**: scale applied, facing **-Y**, feet at Z=0, centered on X=0, symmetric, in T- or A-pose (A-pose 30–45° deforms shoulders better). Run `blender-asset-qa` first.
2. **Metarig**: `scripts/rigify_build.py -- --add basic_human --fit Body` (`human` adds a full face rig; for games use `--no-face` + shape keys).
3. **Place the joints** (the fit only scales). Edit bones in X-ray against the mesh: joints sit at the **pivot of rotation** (inside the volume, not on the surface). The elbow and knee need a slight bend toward their natural direction (elbow back, knee forward) so the IK solves the right way. Symmetrize: `bpy.ops.armature.symmetrize()`. Check with `look` (`shading="xray"`).
4. **Generate**: `--metarig META_Body --generate` gives `RIG_Body` (control rig: FK/IK, IK/FK snapping, tweak bones, bone collections).
5. **Skin**: `scripts/bind_mesh.py -- --armature RIG_Body --meshes Body`. It uses heat weights, switches to the voxel-proxy transfer automatically when heat fails (non-manifold, kitbashed or AI meshes), then cleans to 4 influences and normalizes.
6. **Stress test**: `scripts/stress_poses.py -- --armature RIG_Body`, then `look(mode="frames", frames=[1,10,20,30,40,50])`. Fix collapsing elbows, candy-wrapped forearms, a sunken shoulder or a hip crease (below).
7. **Engine skeleton**: `rigify_build.py -- --rig RIG_Body --game-skeleton` gives `GAME_RIG_Body` = `root` + DEF bones in a clean hierarchy, with `DEF-` stripped, constrained to the control rig and with the meshes re-targeted. Animate with the control rig, then bake to the game skeleton and export it (`blender-animation` → `blender-export-pipelines`).
8. **Validate**: `scripts/rig_check.py -- --armature GAME_RIG_Body --profile unity|unreal|roblox [--fix]`.

## Bone rules
- **Layers of a production rig**: `DEF` (deforming, the only ones exported), `ORG` (original metarig copy), `MCH` (mechanism helpers), controls (what animators touch). Never weight to control/MCH bones.
- **Naming**: `.L`/`.R` suffixes (mirror tools, Rigify and `rig_check` depend on them). Unique, ASCII. Bone collections (`arm.collections.new("FK")`, `bcoll.assign(bone)`) replace the old bone layers.
- **Roll**: consistent local axes. Y points down the bone; recalc with `armature.calculate_roll(type="GLOBAL_POS_Z")` for limbs, or per chain. Mirrored bones must have mirrored roll (`rig_check` flags this).
- **Chains**: connected parent→child for limbs. Spine 3–5 bones, neck 1–2. Twist bones on the forearm and upper arm (Rigify's `.001` segments) prevent candy-wrapping.
- The root bone sits at the origin, Y-forward, carries no weights, and is used for root motion.
- **Scale**: armature object scale 1, rotation 0. Apply before skinning. Non-uniform bone scale animation breaks engines.

## Weight painting rules (what pros check)
- ≤ 4 influences per vertex (mobile/Roblox), ≤ 8 on PC if the engine supports it. Always normalized. Weights below 0.01 removed.
- **Smooth falloff across joints**: a 50/50 blend at the joint line, fading over ~1–2 edge loops. A hard 1/0 cut shows a crease; too wide gives rubbery limbs.
- **Elbows/knees**: weight the outer side to the upper bone longer so the joint keeps volume. Add a helper/corrective bone or corrective shape for sharp bends.
- **Shoulders**: blend the clavicle, upper arm and spine. Test arms raised above the head (stress frame 10).
- **Hips**: the thigh-pelvis blend in front stays tight (crease) and soft at the back (glutes).
- **Head/neck**: rigid head (100% head bone above the jawline), smooth neck blend. Props (helmets, armor plates) get 100% weight to a single bone, so they stay rigid with no stretching.
- **Mirror**: paint one side, then `object.vertex_group_mirror(all_groups=True, flip_group_names=True, use_topology=False)`, or work with X-mirror on.
- **Tools** (live): Weight Paint mode with auto-normalize on, the gradient tool, Smooth (`vertex_group_smooth`), Levels, and `object.data_transfer` from a good mesh (clothing gets its weights from the body).

## Correctives (beyond weights)
Corrective shape keys driven by bone rotation fix elbows, knees and shoulders in hero rigs. Sculpt the fix in the posed state (`modifier_apply_as_shapekey` or the Corrective Shape Keys add-on approach), then drive the key value from the bone's local rotation (driver `TRANSFORMS` var `ROT_X` in `LOCAL_SPACE`, mapped from 0 at rest to 1 at full bend). Games: correctives export as blendshapes. Drive them in the engine (UE Pose Driver / Unity script) or bake them into the animation.

## Engine skeleton specifics
- **Unity Humanoid**: Hips → Spine → Chest → Neck → Head, plus limbs. The game skeleton maps automatically (`rig_check --profile unity` shows the mapping). T-pose bind pose recommended.
- **Unreal**: retarget to the UE5 Mannequin with IK Retargeter. Matching names (`pelvis`, `spine_01`, `thigh_l`...) speeds up chain mapping (`--profile unreal` lists the gaps). No leaf bones.
- **Roblox R15**: a fixed hierarchy and names (`LowerTorso`, `UpperTorso`, `LeftUpperArm`...), `Root > HumanoidRootNode > LowerTorso`, no weights on Root, ≤ 4 influences. Build it manually or from Roblox's Blender template rather than Rigify. Details are in `blender-export-pipelines/references/roblox.md`.

## Gotchas
- `rigify_generate` needs the metarig **selected and active** (`temp_override` isn't enough). The scripts handle this.
- "Bone Heat Weighting: failed to find solution" comes from non-manifold, intersecting parts or tiny scale. `bind_mesh.py` falls back to proxy. Fix the scale first.
- Meshes parented with "Keep Transform" but with unapplied scale get a double transform. Apply the scale before parenting.
- Modifier order: Armature should come **after** shape-key-like deforms and **before** Subdivision/Corrective Smooth (Corrective Smooth after Armature reduces collapsing).
- 5.0: `bone.select` is gone. Use `pose_bone.select` or `edit_bone.select`. `bone.hide` affects edit bones too.

# Clothing

The execution model is in `blender-core`. The rig and weights are in `blender-character-rigging`, classic cloth settings in `blender-simulation`, and Roblox layered clothing cages in `blender-export-pipelines` (references/roblox.md).

## One call each
```
scripts/garment.py -- --body Body --group Torso --name Shirt --hide-body
scripts/garment.py -- --body Body --zmin 0.45 --zmax 1.05 --name Pants --offset 0.01 --drape 40 --morphs
scripts/garment.py -- --body Body --group Torso --name Armor --offset 0.02 --thickness 0.008
scripts/garment.py -- --check Shirt --body Body          # pose the rig first: checks the current pose
```

## How pros build game clothing
1. **Shape**: start from the body (extract + offset) for fitted clothes, or from flat patterns sewn by cloth sim (Marvelous Designer or Blender cloth with sewing springs) for loose ones. Simulate on the body in its **rest pose** (A/T).
2. **Game mesh**: retopo the high/sim result to clean, even quads with loops at the joints (elbows, knees, shoulders get 3 loops), then UV it. Bake folds into normal maps (`blender-texture-baking`) so the low mesh stays light.
3. **Skin**: copy weights from the body (same bones, same influences), clean them (limit 4, normalize, drop < 0.001), then blend toward smoother weights only on loose parts (skirts, coats) and add extra bones for those.
4. **Hide what's covered**: delete body faces under the garment (save tris, stop poke-through) or mask them per outfit. Keep one ring of skin under cuffs and collars.
5. **Verify in motion**: stress poses (`blender-character-rigging` `stress_poses.py`), then `--check` in each. Fix by easing (offset), smoothing the body there, weight tweaks, or hiding.

## garment.py
- Region: `--group` (body vertex group, weight > 0.5) or a world `--zmin/--zmax` band. The faces are copied in world space and pushed out along the vertex normals by `--offset` (ease: 5–10 mm fitted cotton, 10–20 mm jackets, 15–30 mm armor). Then `Solidify` adds `--thickness` (2–4 mm fabric, 5–10 mm leather/armor), growing outward. UVs carry over from the body.
- Weights: Data Transfer (`POLYINTERP_NEAREST`, all groups by name), applied, limited to `--max-influences`, normalized and cleaned. The body's Armature modifier is added and parented to the rig.
- `--hide-body`: `Hidden_<name>` vertex group (the region shrunk by one ring) + an inverted Mask modifier on the body. Swappable outfits toggle masks. For export, delete those faces on a body copy instead.
- `--drape N`: classic cloth (cotton-ish: mass 0.15, tension 15, bending 0.5, quality 8). The top 8% is pinned, the body collides at 3 mm, it settles N frames, then the result is applied. That gives gravity folds on loose areas. Use 30–60 frames.
- `--morphs`: for each body shape key, a same-named garment shape key, via Surface Deform bound in the rest pose and applied as a shape key per morph. Engines drive body and garment keys together (fat/thin, muscle, breathing). Measured: a 30% body morph pokes through 346 verts. With the matching garment key, 0.
- **Poke check** (also run at the end of every build): casts along each body vertex normal. If the garment is hit inward before outward (or sits < 0.5 mm away), it's poke-through. Verts that hit no garment within 0.1 m aren't covered and are ignored. It reports `covered_verts`, `poke_verts` and `poke_max_m`, uses the **evaluated** pose, and respects the body masks.

## Layered clothing
- Order from the skin out: underwear/base → shirt → vest → jacket → armor. Each layer offsets from the one below (run `garment.py --body Shirt` for a vest over the shirt) and copies weights from the body, not from the layer below.
- Interpenetration between layers in motion usually comes from mismatched weights. Copying all layers from the same body keeps them moving together.
- Roblox layered clothing needs `<Name>_InnerCage` + `<Name>_OuterCage` built from Roblox's template cages (same vert order/UVs). Other engines (UE Mutable/Unity) blend shape keys or use body-hiding masks. Same principle.

## Gotchas
- `shape_key_add()` creates keys at value 1.0 (measured). Set `.value = 0` when authoring morphs from Python.
- Surface Deform for **morphs only**: if left live together with an Armature modifier, the pose is applied twice. `--morphs` removes it after baking the keys.
- Apply the body's scale before building. Offsets and thickness are in meters.
- Cloth sims need the body's collision mesh at a modest resolution. Decimate a proxy for the collision if the body is > 50k verts.
- Run `blender-asset-qa` on the final garment (z-fighting with the body, floating parts, normals) and check its tris against `blender-game-optimization` budgets.

# Blender Core (5.2 LTS+)

## Route to the specialized skill
| Task | Skill |
|---|---|
| Units, collections, naming, linking, asset libraries | `blender-scene-setup` |
| Hard-surface modeling, bevels, booleans, normals | `blender-hardsurface-modeling` |

| Batch/headless pipelines, file conversion | `blender-pipeline-automation` |
| Checking a mesh/asset before delivery (always) | `blender-asset-qa` |
| End-to-end playbooks (prop, character, Roblox, product shot) | `blender-workflow-recipes` |

## Execute
**Live (blender-mcp `execute_blender_code`)**: work in small steps and print only what you need. To call a skill script, import it:
```python
import sys, importlib; sys.path.insert(0, r"<skills_dir>/blender-asset-qa/scripts")
import qa_check; importlib.reload(qa_check); print(qa_check.run(objects=["Chair"]))
```
Each MCP call runs in a **fresh namespace**: re-`import` in every call. That's cheap because modules stay cached in `sys.modules`. `reload` only after editing a script.
**Headless (any agent with a shell)**: this prints only the script's JSON (`@@JSON@@` lines):
```
python <skills_dir>/blender-core/scripts/run_in_blender.py --blend in.blend <script.py> -- --objects Chair --save out.blend
python <skills_dir>/blender-core/scripts/run_in_blender.py --expr "import bpy; print(len(bpy.data.objects))"
```
Raw form: `blender -b in.blend --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 -P x.py -- args`. Every script here exposes `run(**kw) -> dict` and the same flags after `--`.
**First call in a session**: `scripts/env_report.py`, which returns the version, engines, GPU, add-ons, units, color management and scene counts.

## Rules
- **Data API over operators**: use `bpy.data`, `bmesh`, `mesh.attributes`, and `foreach_get/set` with numpy. Operators depend on context and selection, and many need a 3D View, which background mode doesn't have.
- If an operator is unavoidable: `with bpy.context.temp_override(object=ob, active_object=ob, selected_objects=[ob], selected_editable_objects=[ob]): bpy.ops...`. Check that the result is `{'FINISHED'}`.
- **Edit mode isolation**: `ob.data` isn't updated while in Edit Mode. Use `bmesh.from_edit_mesh` + `bmesh.update_edit_mesh`, or switch to OBJECT mode before reading.
- **Nodes**: find them by `type` (`n.type == "BSDF_PRINCIPLED"`), never by `name`, because names are localized. Sockets by English name or `identifier` are fine.
- **Enums**: read the valid values with `[i.identifier for i in T.bl_rna.properties[p].enum_items]`. Dynamic enums (`render.engine`, `view_transform`, `look`) under-report, so assign them inside `try/except TypeError` (the message lists the valid values).
- **Engines**: `BLENDER_EEVEE`, `CYCLES`, `BLENDER_WORKBENCH`. Cycles device: `scene.cycles.device = "GPU"` + preferences `compute_device_type`.
- **Evaluated data**: use `ob.evaluated_get(depsgraph)`, then `.to_mesh()`, then always `.to_mesh_clear()`. Call `view_layer.update()` before reading `matrix_world` after a change.
- **Freed data**: applying or removing a modifier, or removing an object or ID, frees it. Collect names first (`[m.name for m in ob.modifiers]`) and never touch the old Python reference afterward, because it returns garbage or crashes.
- **Never trust default names** ("Cube.001"). Keep object references, rename explicitly, and look objects up via `bpy.data.objects[name]`.
- **Scale**: 1 unit = 1 m. Apply rotation/scale (`transform_apply`) before bevels, modifiers with distances, rigging, physics, baking and export.
- **Paths**: `bpy.path.abspath("//textures/x.png")` resolves relative to the .blend. Save explicitly; use `save_as_mainfile(filepath=..., copy=True)` for backups.
- **Live sessions are the user's work**: never `read_factory_settings`, never delete data you didn't create, and save a backup copy before destructive batch edits.
- **GPU module in background**: call `gpu.init()` first (5.2+). `bgl` no longer exists.
- **Big meshes**: no per-vertex `bpy.ops`. Use numpy `foreach_get` (see references/bpy-patterns.md).

## 5.x API changes that break old tutorials/LLM memory
`action.fcurves` → channelbags · `scene.node_tree` → `scene.compositing_node_group` · `material.use_nodes` is deprecated (new materials already have nodes) · `mod["Socket_2"]` → `mod.properties.inputs.Socket_2.value` (5.2) · `BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT` → `BLENDER_EEVEE` · Boolean `FAST` → `FLOAT` · bone layers → bone collections · `bl_info` add-ons → extensions (`blender_manifest.toml`) · `bpy.props` values are no longer dict-accessible (`scene["cycles"]`). Full table: [references/api-changes-5x.md](references/api-changes-5x.md).

## Verify (required before saying "done")
1. Numbers, not adjectives: report tris, objects, materials, dimensions (`ob.dimensions`) and the output files written.
2. Geometry changed → run `blender-asset-qa` `qa_check.py` (z-fighting, detached parts, non-manifold, flipped normals, scale).
3. Look at it: MCP `look` (`mode="angles"`, shading `material`/`wireframe`). Headless: `blender-asset-qa/scripts/review_shots.py` renders contact sheets.
4. Re-read your own output: confirm that exported files exist and that their size is non-zero.

## References
- [references/api-changes-5x.md](references/api-changes-5x.md): 4.x→5.2 migration table. Load it when code fails with AttributeError/KeyError.
- [references/bpy-patterns.md](references/bpy-patterns.md): verified snippets for bmesh, attributes, numpy, temp_override, depsgraph, drivers, append/link, handlers and timers.

# Environment kits

The execution model is in `blender-core`. Custom GN tools are in `blender-geometry-nodes`, materials in `blender-texturing` (trims, vertex blends), and mood/weather in `blender-time-of-day`/`blender-weather-fx`.

## One call each
```
scripts/terrain.py -- --size 400 --res 513 --height 60 --type ridged --erosion 30 --flatten 0 0 40 --material
scripts/terrain.py -- --heightmap //hm.png --size 1000 --res 1009 --height 120 --export-splat //T_Splat.png
scripts/scatter.py -- --target Terrain --collection Trees --density 0.02 --min-distance 5 --max-slope 25 --height-max 45
scripts/scatter.py -- --target Terrain --collection Rocks --density 0.05 --max-slope 70 --align 0.8 --name ENV_Rocks
scripts/kit_check.py -- --objects SM_Wall_4m SM_Floor_4m SM_Door_4m --grid 0.5 --fix
```

## Terrain (terrain.py)
- Grid of `--res`² verts over `--size` m. Use **2^n + 1** for Unity (513/1025/2049, `.raw` 16-bit LE) and UE Landscape's recommended sizes (505/1009/2017/4033, 16-bit PNG). Above 1025, tile it.
- `--type fbm` (rolling), `ridged` (mountains), `hills` (hetero terrain). `--scale` = feature size m. `--erosion N` = thermal erosion steps (talus 33°): slopes relax and debris fills valleys. `--terrace` m = stepped flats. `--flatten X Y R` = a level play/build area blended back with a smoothstep.
- Writes `ENV_Slope` (deg/90) and `ENV_Height` (0–1) point attributes. `--material` builds grass/rock/snow from them: rock above 35°, snow above 75% height on slopes below ~40°, with noise-broken edges.
- Engines: `--export-heightmap` (PNG = 16-bit gray, `.raw` = 16-bit little-endian, row 0 = −Y edge; flip vertically in Unity if mirrored) plus `heightmap_z_scale_m` for the import Z scale. `--export-splat` = 16-bit RGBA weights (R grass, G rock, B snow, sum 1) for terrain layers. Both are written Raw (no display transform): measured round-trip error < 0.001.

## Scatter (scatter.py)
- One GN modifier per layer: Poisson disk (`--density` per m² max, `--min-distance` m), kept where the **interpolated surface normal** is within `--max-slope` and Z is inside `--height-min/max` (object space). `--mask` = vertex group or float attribute as density factor (paint it, or use `ENV_Height`).
- Collection children are instanced at their own origins with random yaw, `--scale` range, and `--align` (0 = upright trees, 0.6–1 = rocks hugging the slope). The source collection is excluded from the view layer.
- The result checks every instance against the real surface (`slope_max_deg`, `height_range`) and counts per source. Instances stay instances. `--realize` only when an exporter or boolean needs real mesh.
- Densities: forest trees 0.01–0.05/m² (min distance 4–8 m), bushes 0.05–0.2, rocks 0.01–0.1, grass clumps 2–20/m² (near camera only). Layer big → small: trees, then bushes masked away from trunks, then grass.
- Engines: glTF `export_gpu_instances=True` (EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing), or `--export-points file.json` (world transforms, Z-up m, wxyz quats) for UE foliage/PCG or Unity instancing scripts. FBX needs realized geometry or one object per instance.

## Modular kits (kit_check.py)
- **Metrics first**: pick a grid (0.5 m snap, 1/2/4 m modules) and keep it everywhere. Walls 3–4 m tall interior (player ~1.8 m eye 1.6 m, doors ≥ 1 × 2.2 m), floors 4 × 4 m, stairs 0.18 m rise / 0.28 m run. UE works in cm (×100 on import), Unity in m.
- **Pivot** convention (`--pivot corner` default, `bottom-center`, `center`) so pieces snap by increments. Footprint lengths are multiples of the grid. Thinner-than-a-cell dims (wall thickness, trims) may be off-grid.
- Open edges only on the piece's outer faces (seams); holes inside are errors. Seam verts must be on the grid so neighbours weld visually. Texel density within 25% of the kit median (`--texture` px). `SM_` names (`--prefix`).
- `--fix` applies rotation/scale and moves each origin to the pivot without moving geometry. Linked duplicates share mesh data, so fix the source once.
- Break repetition with trims and decals (`blender-texturing`), vertex-color blends, and rotated/mirrored variants (mirrors flip normals, so check with `blender-asset-qa`). Hide seams with trim pieces over joints.

## Gotchas
- Apply terrain/kit scale before scattering. Densities and slopes are world-based.
- Scatter height is in the target's object space. Keep terrains at the origin or offset `--height-*`.
- Huge Poisson counts are slow. Scatter per tile/area, or lower the density in the viewport and raise it for renders.
- Validate terrain + scatter with `blender-asset-qa` (floating instances on cliffs, z-fighting decals) and `blender-game-optimization` (instances, LODs, draw calls).

# Export Pipelines

The execution model is in `blender-core`. Run `blender-asset-qa` (and `blender-game-optimization` for budgets) **before** exporting.

## One call
```
scripts/export_asset.py -- --preset unreal_skeletal --objects SK_Hero --out //export/SK_Hero.fbx
scripts/export_asset.py -- --preset web --collection Export --out //export/scene.glb
scripts/export_asset.py -- --preset unity --objects SM_A SM_B SM_C --batch --out //export/x.fbx   # one file each, at origin
```
Presets: `roblox`, `roblox_gltf`, `unity`, `unity_skeletal`, `unreal`, `unreal_skeletal`, `godot`, `web`, `gltf`, `usd`. Pass any exporter kwarg with `--set key=value`. Every preset is tested with a round-trip that keeps scale and avoids a 100× armature scale.

## Engine reference (load only the one you need)
- [references/roblox.md](references/roblox.md): MeshParts, avatar bodies (R15), accessories, layered clothing cages, SurfaceAppearance, limits
- [references/unity.md](references/unity.md): FBX settings, Humanoid rigs, URP/HDRP maps, animation clips
- [references/unreal.md](references/unreal.md): static/skeletal FBX, root bone, collision UCX, LODs, Nanite, ORM/DirectX
- [references/godot-web.md](references/godot-web.md): glTF/GLB, import suffixes, three.js/Babylon, compression, KHR extensions

## Universal pre-export checklist
1. **Scale**: scene unit scale 1.0, objects at scale 1, rotation applied (except intentional object transforms). The presets handle unit conversion.
2. **Pivot/origin** where the engine expects it: props at the bottom-center, characters at the world origin between the feet, facing **-Y** (Blender front). Every preset converts that to the engine's forward.
3. **Modifiers**: the presets export the evaluated mesh. Mirror, bevel and weighted normals are kept; booleans become real geometry.
4. **Normals**: custom/weighted normals export. Smooth shading, plus hard edges marked sharp.
5. **Triangulation**: FBX presets triangulate (`use_triangles`) so the bake and engine tangents match. glTF always triangulates.
6. **Materials**: image-texture → Principled chains only, with names `M_*` and textures `T_*`. Procedural nodes don't export, so bake them first.
7. **Armature**: deform bones only, no leaf bones, rest pose = bind pose, 4 weights per vertex max, and the root at the origin.
8. **Animation**: one action per clip, named `Rig_Clip`. Bake constraints/IK to keys (`blender-animation`). FBX exports the active/NLA action per preset settings; glTF `ACTIONS` mode exports every action that has a slot for the armature.
9. **Naming**: unique, ASCII, no spaces. Engines key materials/meshes by name across reimports.

## Format choice
| Need | Format |
|---|---|
| Unity, Unreal (most stable for skeletal) | FBX |
| Godot, web, Roblox (supported), Unreal 5.x Interchange, Blender↔Blender | glTF 2.0 (`.glb`) |
| Film/VFX, Omniverse, Apple AR (`.usdz`), layout interchange | USD |
| Static geometry for printing/CAD | OBJ / STL (`wm.obj_export`, `wm.stl_export`) |
| Point caches / deforming sims | Alembic (`wm.alembic_export`) |

## Verify after export (required)
- The script returns `ok`, the file size, and for `.glb` a parsed summary (meshes, materials, images, animations, skins, tris, extensions). Compare it with what you expected.
- For FBX/USD: re-import into an empty scene (`import_scene.fbx` / `wm.usd_import`) and check `dimensions`, the armature scale (must be 1, not 100) and the action count.
- In the engine: scale against a reference (UE mannequin 180 cm, Unity capsule 2 m, Roblox character 5 studs), normals/smoothing, the normal map's green channel, and animation root motion.

## Collection exporters (re-export in one click, 4.2+)
See `blender-scene-setup`: `collection.exporters` stores the format + settings per collection, and `bpy.ops.wm.collection_export_all()` re-exports everything.

## Gotchas
- FBX `use_tspace` fails silently on n-gons. Triangulate first (the presets do).
- `bake_space_transform` (Apply Transform) is experimental. Use it for Unity static meshes only, never with armatures.
- glTF exports **actions** linked through slots/NLA. An action with no user on the armature is skipped (`export_animation_mode` options: `ACTIONS`, `ACTIVE_ACTIONS`, `NLA_TRACKS`, `SCENE`, `BROADCAST`).
- glTF needs image textures in PNG/JPEG/WebP. EXR/TIFF get converted (`export_image_format`).
- Linked library data exports fine, but make it local or override it if you need to modify it first.
- Shape keys: FBX exports them as blendshapes, glTF as morph targets (`export_morph`). Modifiers before the Armature modifier can block shape-key export in FBX (apply them first).

# Facial Rig & Shape Keys

The execution model is in `blender-core`. The body rig is in `blender-character-rigging`.

## Choose the approach
| Approach | Use | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Blendshapes (ARKit 52)** | games, VTubers, mocap (iPhone/Live Link Face), web/VRM | the industry interchange set; each shape is sculpted |
| **Bones** (jaw, eyes, lids, brows, lips) | stylized, low memory, mobile | jaw + eyes as bones are almost always right |
| **Hybrid** | most production game heads | jaw/eye/tongue bones + blendshapes for everything soft |
| **Rigify face** (`human` metarig) | film-style keyframe animation inside Blender | 100+ face bones, heavy for engines |

## Procedure (blendshapes)
1. The head mesh needs clean loops around the eyes and mouth (`blender-retopology-uv`), with eyes, teeth and tongue as separate objects parented or weighted to bones.
2. `scripts/shapekeys.py -- --mesh Head --create arkit` (or `--create visemes` for the 15 Oculus visemes) creates empty, correctly named keys.
3. Sculpt each key (live: sculpt mode on the active key, `use_shape_key_edit_mode`). Symmetric expressions can be sculpted once, then `--split eyeBlink` gives `eyeBlinkLeft/Right` with a soft blend across X=0 (`--falloff` m).
4. `--mirror browDownLeft` builds `browDownRight` (topology-independent mirror).
5. `--report` lists unsculpted keys, the max offset per key, and missing ARKit names. A shape is done only when every key moves and nothing is left over.
6. Optional: `--drivers FaceCtrl` adds a controller with 0–1 custom properties driving each key, for keyframing in Blender.
7. Check the extremes and **combinations** (jawOpen + mouthSmile, eyeBlink + eyeSquint) with `look`. Fix them with corrective combination keys driven by the product of two keys.

## Shape key rules
- Shapes are **deltas from Basis**. Never change the Basis topology after creating keys (adding or removing verts destroys every key).
- One action per key. No head or neck movement inside face keys (bones do that). Keep eyelids sliding over the eye surface, not through it (check with `blender-asset-qa` zfighting on lid/eye).
- Range 0–1. `slider_max` can be raised for exaggeration, but engines clamp to 0–1.
- Relative keys (`use_relative=True`, the default) are the only kind that exports.
- Name exactly per spec (case-sensitive): `eyeBlinkLeft`, not `EyeBlink_L`. Engines map by name.
- Keys on meshes with Subdivision: sculpt at level 0, and keep the subdivision modifier **after** the shape keys (they're evaluated first anyway).
- Applying modifiers on a mesh with shape keys fails. Use `modifier_apply_as_shapekey` for deform modifiers, or apply them before creating keys.

## Correctives and combination shapes
- Corrective for a bone pose: sculpt in the posed state, then drive with a `TRANSFORMS` variable (`ROT_X`, `LOCAL_SPACE`, mapped to 0–1).
- Combination: key `jawOpen_mouthSmile` with driver `SCRIPTED` expression `a*b`, from the two key values (`SINGLE_PROP` `key_blocks["jawOpen"].value`). Simple expressions don't need Python auto-run.

## Engine notes
- **Unity**: FBX blendshapes. In the Model importer, set Blend Shape Normals = Calculate (or Import if smoothing was exported). ARKit names map to the AR Foundation face-tracking samples.
- **Unreal**: morph targets ("Import Morph Targets"). Live Link Face / MetaHuman Animator use ARKit names, and the Pose Asset maps the curves. No leaf bones.
- **Roblox dynamic heads**: FACS-based poses with Roblox-specific names, authored as animation frames on a head rig (Creator Hub "Dynamic heads" spec). Build from the official Blender template. ARKit sculpts can be reused by renaming/mapping. Head ≤ 4,000 tris.
- **VRM / web (three-vrm, ReadyPlayerMe-style)**: ARKit 52 + visemes as glTF morph targets (`export_morph=True`). Keep the morph-normal export on only if shading needs it (it doubles the size).
- Drop unused keys before export. Every key costs memory per vertex (glTF sparse accessors help).

## Gotchas
- `ob.shape_key_add(from_mix=False)` copies the Basis. `from_mix=True` bakes the current mix (useful for combos, dangerous by accident).
- `shape_key_mirror(use_topology=False)` needs a mesh symmetric on X. Run it on the **active** key (the script handles this).
- Driver variables on shape keys use the Key ID (`ob.data.shape_keys`), not the mesh: `fc = kb.driver_add("value")`.

# Game Optimization

The execution model is in `blender-core`. Always re-run `blender-asset-qa` after optimizing.

## Procedure
1. **Measure**: `scripts/mesh_stats.py -- --objects ... --budget mobile|roblox|web|vr|console|pc`. It returns tris, estimated draw calls, materials, texture VRAM, bones, and the over-budget items.
2. **Clean**: `make_lods.py --cleanup` (merge by distance 0.1 mm, dissolve degenerate, delete loose). Remove hidden faces: back-to-back faces and faces under other parts (`qa_check` → `back_to_back`, plus manual xray).
3. **Reduce in this order** (cheapest visual loss first): hidden/interior geometry → unnecessary edge loops on flat areas (Limited Dissolve 1–5°) → over-segmented cylinders → Decimate → bake detail to normals (`blender-texture-baking`).
4. **Materials**: merge to 1–2 per asset (atlas / trim sheet / shared tiling material). Each material slot per mesh is roughly one draw call.
5. **LODs**: `scripts/make_lods.py -- --objects SM_X --rename` creates `_LOD1.._LOD3` at 50/25/12.5%. Check every LOD silhouette with `look`/`review_shots`.
6. **Re-measure**, then QA, then export (`blender-export-pipelines`).

## Budgets (guidance per asset, 2026)
| Platform | Hero char tris | Prop tris | Mats/asset | Max texture | Bones |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mobile | 5–15k | 0.3–3k | 1–2 | 1024 | ≤75 |
| Roblox | body ≤10,742 (head 4k, torso 1.75k, limb 1,248); accessory/clothing 4k | ≤20k per MeshPart | 1 (SurfaceAppearance) | 1024 (PBR), 4k max | R15 + optional |
| Web (three.js/Babylon) | 10–30k | 1–10k | 1–2 | 2048 | ≤100 |
| Standalone VR (Quest) | 10–40k | 1–10k | 1–3 | 2048 | ≤100 |
| Console / PC | 50–150k | 5–50k | 2–6 | 4096 | 150–300 |
| UE5 Nanite (static) | — | millions OK | few | 4096+ | n/a |
Whole-scene limits matter more than single assets: mobile ≈ 100–300k tris visible and < 100–200 draw calls; PC ≈ millions of tris and < 2–5k draw calls.

## Decimate modes
| Mode | Use | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `COLLAPSE` (ratio) | organic, scans, LODs | `use_symmetry`, vertex group factor to protect faces/hands; triangulates |
| `UNSUBDIV` (iterations) | meshes made by subdividing quads | restores the quad grid cleanly |
| `DISSOLVE` (planar, angle) | hard-surface / CAD | delimit `{"SEAM","SHARP","MATERIAL","UV"}`; keeps the silhouette, makes n-gons → triangulate on export |
Protect UV seams and silhouette: decimate a copy, then compare. If UVs tear at LOD1, the ratio is too aggressive for that topology, so re-unwrap or use a manual LOD.

## The hidden cost: vertex splits
GPU vertex count = unique (position, normal, UV, color) combinations. Every UV seam and hard edge **duplicates** vertices, so engine vertex counts are often 1.5–3× Blender's. Minimize seams where they aren't needed, keep hard edges = seams (so the split happens once), and don't add vertex colors or extra UV sets you don't use.

## LOD rules
- Halve the tris per level. Switch at screen size ~0.5 / 0.25 / 0.125 (UE "Screen Size", Unity LOD Group %, Godot `lod_bias` auto).
- LODs keep the same materials (or fewer: merge them at LOD2+), same pivot, same bounds.
- Skeletal LODs: remove finger/face bones at LOD2+ (the engine bone-reduction tools handle this). Keep the skinning on the same skeleton.
- Far LOD / foliage: impostor/billboard. Unreal Nanite (static, opaque/masked) and Godot's auto mesh LOD can replace a hand-made chain.
- Roblox: no manual LODs. `RenderFidelity=Automatic` does it. Keep each MeshPart ≤ 20k tris and use a simple `CollisionFidelity` (Box/Hull) for non-walkable parts.

## Draw calls and batching
- **Merge** static meshes that share a material and are always seen together (join objects). **Don't merge** across large areas, because that defeats frustum/occlusion culling.
- **Instancing**: repeated objects as linked duplicates (Alt+D, shared mesh) or collection instances. They export as instances (glTF `EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing` with `export_gpu_instances`) or as one mesh + transforms in the engine.
- **Atlases/trim sheets**: put many props on one texture set. Trim sheets let walls, panels and pipes share one 2k material.
- **Texture memory** (upper bound, uncompressed RGBA8 + mips): 1k = 5.3 MB, 2k = 21 MB, 4k = 85 MB. Engines compress (BC7/ASTC ≈ 4–8×). Pack grayscale maps into ORM channels to cut it 3×.

## Collision
Keep collision separate and simple: boxes/convex hulls of ≤ 32–255 verts. UE `UCX_<Mesh>_##`, Godot `-colonly`/`-convcolonly` suffix, Unity MeshCollider on a simplified mesh, Roblox `CollisionFidelity`. Never use the render mesh as a physics mesh for anything that moves.

## Rig and animation cost
Limit to 4 influences per vertex (`vertex_group_limit_total(limit=4)` + normalize). Remove non-deforming bones from the export (`use_armature_deform_only`). Bake constraints and drivers to keys. Shape keys cost memory per vertex, so drop unused ones and keep only deltas (glTF sparse accessors handle this).

## Gotchas
- Decimate on meshes with unapplied modifiers: `make_lods.py` evaluates them first. Other paths need you to apply them.
- Join (`Ctrl+J`) merges materials and UV maps by **name**. Rename the UV maps identically first, or the UVs get lost.
- The `Weld` modifier is the non-destructive merge by distance. Use `mode="CONNECTED"` to avoid welding separate parts.
- Triangulate before measuring if the engine will. Quads already count as 2 tris in the stats.

# Geometry Nodes

The execution model is in `blender-core`. Build trees with `scripts/gn_builder.py`, a compact JSON spec that's far cheaper than raw bpy. Look up exact socket names first, because they change between versions:
```
scripts/gn_builder.py -- --describe GeometryNodeDistributePointsOnFaces GeometryNodeInstanceOnPoints
scripts/gn_builder.py -- --spec scatter.json --apply Ground --set Density=20 Seed=3 Mask=@paint_mask
```
`--set Name=@attr` feeds a modifier input from a named attribute. The result reports evaluated vert/face counts and node warnings. The spec format is in the script docstring; full examples are in [references/recipes.md](references/recipes.md).

## Core concepts (get these right or nothing works)
- **Geometry** flows left→right through sockets with **circle** shapes. **Fields** (diamond sockets) are functions evaluated per element **on the node that consumes them**, in that node's domain/context.
- **Domains**: Point, Edge, Face, Face Corner, Spline, Instance, Layer. `Capture Attribute` freezes a field at a point in the graph (before topology changes), and `Evaluate on Domain` converts between domains.
- **Attributes**: built-ins (`position`, `normal`, `sharp_face`, `material_index`, `UVMap`...) plus named ones via `Store Named Attribute`. Named attributes persist after the modifier. That's how GN data reaches shaders (Attribute node) and exporters (glTF `export_attributes`, which exports names starting with `_`).
- **Instances** are cheap (one mesh, many transforms). **Realize Instances** only when you must edit per-instance geometry or export a single mesh. Realize as late as possible.
- Inputs exposed on the group interface become **modifier inputs** (5.2: `mod.properties.inputs.<identifier>.value`). Panels group them, menu sockets give enums.

## Zones and advanced types
| Feature | Nodes | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Simulation zone | `GeometryNodeSimulationInput/Output` (paired) | per-frame state: growth, particles, erosion; bake to keep |
| Repeat zone | `GeometryNodeRepeatInput/Output` | iterate N times (L-systems, relaxation, recursive subdivision) |
| For Each Element | `GeometryNodeForeachGeometryElementInput/Output` | run a sub-graph per element (per building lot, per island) |
| Closures / Bundles (5.0+) | `NodeClosureInput/Output`, `NodeCombineBundle`/`NodeSeparateBundle`, Evaluate Closure | pass functions/structured data around; reusable "strategy" node groups |
| Lists (5.2) | `GeometryNodeFieldToList`, `ListGetItem`, `ListLength`, `SortList`, `FilterList` | real arrays, not fields |
| Grids/SDF (4.x–5.x) | `MeshToSDFGrid`, `SDFGridBoolean`, `SDFGridFillet`, `SDFGridOffset`, `GridToMesh` | smooth booleans, remeshing, fillets, voxel effects |
| Physics (5.2, experimental) | `GeometryNodeXPBDSolver` + bundles | node-based cloth/hair, see `blender-simulation` |
| Gizmos | `GizmoLinear/Dial/Transform` | viewport handles for inputs |
Zones need `input.pair_with_output(output)` (spec key `pairs`), plus items on the output node (`repeat_items`, `state_items`, ...; spec 4th node field).

## Procedure
1. Sketch the data flow: source geometry → selection/masks (fields) → generate/instance → transform/randomize → realize/merge → set materials/shading → output.
2. `--describe` every node type you'll use, then write the spec and build. Check `node_warnings` and the evaluated counts.
3. Expose only meaningful inputs (density, seed, scale range, materials), with min/max set.
4. Look at it (`look`), check `blender-asset-qa` if the result will be exported (realized geometry), and check `blender-game-optimization` for instance counts and tris.
5. Ship: either keep it procedural (the .blend/asset library), or apply the modifier / `visual_geometry_to_objects` for exporters.

## Rules
- Randomness: always expose a `Seed`, and use `Random Value` with the ID/Index field so results stay stable when counts change.
- Scale-independent setups use `Object Info` (Relative) and real units. Apply the object scale or read it explicitly.
- Materials: `Set Material` inside the tree. The material must exist in the file, and instances keep their own materials.
- Shading: GN output loses auto-smooth unless you add `Set Shade Smooth` + (5.x) the `Smooth by Angle` essentials group, or store `sharp_edge`.
- UVs: primitives output `UVMap` via their UV output. Store it with `Store Named Attribute` (Face Corner, 2D Vector, name `UVMap`) or it's dropped.
- Performance: avoid realizing millions of instances, prefer Points + instances for scatter, use `Merge by Distance` sparingly, and simulation zones need baking for playback/export (`object.geometry_node_bake_single` or modifier `bakes`).
- Node tools (`ng.is_tool = True`, `is_mode_edit` etc.) turn a group into an operator in the 3D View menus, for editing workflows.

## Gotchas
- 5.2: `mod["Socket_2"]` no longer works. Use `getattr(mod.properties.inputs, ident).value`, and `.type = "ATTRIBUTE"` + `.attribute_name` for attribute inputs. Compare and Random Value **sockets changed**: Random Value now has single dynamic `Min`/`Max`/`Value` sockets typed by `data_type`. Link by name, and `--describe` when unsure.
- Sockets that are disabled for the current mode/data type are still in `node.inputs` with the same name. The builder picks the **enabled** one. Set `data_type`/`mode` props first (the builder sets props before links).
- `nt.interface.new_socket(...)` is the 4.0+ API (`ng.inputs.new` is gone).
- Exporters see the **evaluated** mesh. Instances become glTF instancing (`export_gpu_instances`) or are realized on export.

# Hair grooming

The execution model is in `blender-core`. Hair physics details are in `blender-simulation`, and look-dev in `blender-lighting-lookdev`.

## One call each
```
scripts/groom.py -- --surface Head --mask Scalp --length 0.15 --children 150000 --clump 0.5
scripts/groom.py -- --surface Head --mask Beard --length 0.02 --droop 0.2 --curl 0.004 --melanin 0.9 --name Beard
scripts/groom.py -- --surface Body --length 0.025 --droop 0.3 --clump 0.3 --name Fur
scripts/groom.py -- --cards Hair --card-count 150 --atlas-res 2048 --out //textures      # game hair cards
```

## How pros groom
1. **Surface first**: the scalp is a mesh (or the head itself) with **UVs** (hair attaches by UV) and a **vertex group** painted where hair grows. That group becomes the density mask, so soft edges give a natural hairline.
2. **Guides → children**: a few hundred to a few thousand guides carry the shape, and thousands of interpolated children give the volume. Style the guides, never the children.
3. **Shape in layers**: length, then clump (strands gather into locks), then curl/wave, then frizz/noise, then profile (thin tips). Keep each a separate modifier you can toggle.
4. **Comb by hand** for anything hero: Curves Sculpt mode brushes (`Comb`, `Add`, `Puff`, `Pinch`, `Grow/Shrink`, `Smooth`, `Slide`, `Density`, `Delete`, `Pull Tips`). Procedural droop gives a believable base, not a hairstyle.
5. Look-dev under the final lights. Hair reads mostly from **specular** and depth (clumps catch highlights), not albedo.

## groom.py
- Runs 5.2's Add Empty Hair (`object.curves_empty_hair_add`). It parents to the surface, sets `surface`/`surface_uv_map`, adds **Capture Rest Geometry** to the surface, and adds the node **Hair Dynamics** modifier (pinned last, experimental). Then it stacks the bundled assets: Generate (`--density` guides/m²) → Interpolate (`--children`/m², `--viewport` fraction in the viewport) → Clump → Curl → Displace + Shrinkwrap (`--droop` × length down, kept 2 mm above the surface) → Noise → Set Hair Curve Profile (`--radius`, tip taper).
- **Clump/curl guide distance = 10% of `--length`.** The asset's default 0.1 m collapses a whole head into a few tufts.
- Each asset stays a modifier with live inputs, so tweak there. Inputs by name: `getattr(md.properties.inputs, identifier).value`; vertex-group masks use `.type = "ATTRIBUTE"`, `.attribute_name`.
- It reports curves, mean length, the max root gap to the surface (must be ~0) and the modifier stacks. Evaluated counts in background mode use the viewport amount.

## Numbers
| | Value |
|---|---|
| Human scalp | ~100–150k hairs, ~200/cm². CG: 30k–150k rendered strands, 300–3000 guides |
| Strand radius | real 0.03–0.05 mm. Use 0.05 mm (`--radius 0.00005`), thicker with fewer strands |
| Melanin (Principled Hair, Chiang) | black 1.0 · dark brown 0.8 · brown 0.65 · light brown 0.45 · blond 0.25 · platinum 0.1. Red: 0.5 + redness 0.9. Grey: 0 + tint |
| Roughness | 0.25–0.35 (glossy) … 0.5 (dry). Radial roughness 0.3 |
| Fur | length 1–5 cm, density 200k–2M/m², little clump |
`HUANG` (4.0+) models elliptical cross-sections and is better for close-ups. `CHIANG` is the reference default.

## Game hair cards (`--cards HAIR`)
- Picks `--card-count` well-spread strands (farthest-point sampling) of the evaluated groom and builds a ribbon along each: `--card-width` m, tapering to 30% at the tip, lying flat on the surface (side = tangent × surface normal). UV v runs root 0 → tip 1, one atlas column per card (`--atlas-columns`).
- Renders the atlas with Cycles from flat strand clumps: `T_<name>_BC` (darker roots, coverage in alpha, Standard view), plus `T_<name>_RootTip` and `T_<name>_ID` (Raw, linear data). The card material uses Dithered alpha with no backface culling.
- Pros layer cards from the scalp outward: dense, wide, opaque cards on the scalp to hide skin; mid layers; then thin flyaway cards on top. Budgets: hero 20k–60k tris, NPC 5k–15k. Bend cards in S/C shapes, never flat planes, and check from every angle. Engines use alpha test/dither + depth prepass, root-tip for darkening/AO and ID for per-strand variation. Add a tangent (flow) map along V for anisotropic specular.

## Export grooms
Strand hair for UE Groom/Houdini: Alembic (`wm.alembic_export`) or USD (`wm.usd_export(export_curves=True)`). Both write the evaluated curves (measured: 246/246 curves round-trip). Bake the modifier stack first if the target needs guides only.

## Gotchas
- No UVs on the surface means `Generate` has nothing to attach to. Add UVs before grooming.
- Changing the surface topology after grooming breaks attachment. Groom last, or re-run.
- Scale: apply the head's scale. Lengths and densities are world meters.
- Viewport: keep `--viewport` ≤ 0.2 on full heads. Final strand counts only appear in renders.
- Hair Dynamics simulates on playback. For stills on frame 1 it's a pass-through. Bake it (`blender-simulation`) before animated renders.
